\begin{frame}{Two-way tables and marginal frequencies}
A qualitative variable describes a category. It is nominal if its categories have no natural order (means of transport), ordinal if they are ordered (level of satisfaction).
A two-way table counts individuals according to two variables. The sums of the rows and columns are the margins. A marginal frequency divides a margin by the total count.
\end{frame}
\begin{frame}{Two-way tables and marginal frequencies}
In a population of \(100\) individuals, two characteristics \(A,B\) are observed:
\end{frame}
\begin{frame}{Worked answer: Two-way tables and marginal frequencies}
\(f(A)=32/100=0.32\); \(f(B)=35/100=0.35\); \(f(\overline B)=65/100=0.65\). The frequency of \(A\cap B\) is \(20/100=0.20\); it is not a marginal frequency.
\end{frame}
\begin{frame}{Two-way tables and marginal frequencies}
A première class of \(32\) students is split as follows. Complete the margins and calculate the marginal frequencies “CS” and “girls”.
\end{frame}
\begin{frame}{Worked answer: Two-way tables and marginal frequencies}
\(f(\mathrm{CS})=21/32=65.625\%\); \(f(\mathrm{girls})=14/32=43.75\%\).
\end{frame}
\begin{frame}{Conditional frequencies and reading sentences}
The frequency of \(A\) among the individuals of \(B\), if this subpopulation is nonempty, is
\[f_B(A)=\dfrac{\text{count satisfying }A\text{ and }B}{\text{count of }B}.\]
The denominator corresponds to the population introduced by “among”.
\end{frame}
\begin{frame}{Conditional frequencies and reading sentences}
In the CS table, calculate the frequency of girls among the students without CS, then the frequency of students without CS among the girls. Are the two results equal?
\end{frame}
\begin{frame}{Worked answer: Conditional frequencies and reading sentences}
Among the \(11\) students without CS, \(5\) are girls: \(5/11\approx45.45\%\). Among the \(14\) girls, \(5\) do not take CS: \(5/14\approx35.71\%\). The numerator is the same, the reference populations differ.
\end{frame}
\begin{frame}{Conditional frequencies and reading sentences}
In the table of \(100\) individuals, calculate \(f_B(A)\), \(f_A(B)\) and \(f_{\overline A}(B)\). Translate each result into a sentence.
\end{frame}
\begin{frame}{Worked answer: Conditional frequencies and reading sentences}
\(f_B(A)=20/35=4/7\approx57.14\%\) of the individuals of \(B\) satisfy \(A\). \(f_A(B)=20/32=62.5\%\) of the individuals of \(A\) satisfy \(B\). \(f_{\overline A}(B)=15/68\approx22.06\%\) of the individuals not satisfying \(A\) satisfy \(B\).
\end{frame}
\begin{frame}{Conditional frequencies and reading sentences}
Does “\(60\%\) of cyclists are students” allow us to conclude that \(60\%\) of students are cyclists?
\end{frame}
\begin{frame}{Worked answer: Conditional frequencies and reading sentences}
No. For example, out of \(10\) cyclists, \(6\) are students; if the population has \(100\) students in all, only \(6\%\) of the students are cyclists.
\end{frame}
\begin{frame}{Completing a table from frequencies}
A group has \(200\) people, of whom \(120\) use a bus (\(B\)). Among these \(120\) people, \(75\%\) have a pass (\(A\)). Among the other \(80\), \(25\%\) have a pass.

\begin{enumerate}
\setcounter{enumi}{0}\item Construct the two-way table \(B/\overline B\) and \(A/\overline A\) with its margins.
\item Calculate the marginal frequency of \(A\).
\item Calculate the frequency of \(B\) among \(A\).

\end{enumerate}
\end{frame}
\begin{frame}{Worked answer: Completing a table from frequencies}
In \(B\), \(120\times0.75=90\) people satisfy \(A\), so \(30\) do not. In \(\overline B\), \(80\times0.25=20\) satisfy \(A\), and \(60\) do not.
 \begin{center}\begin{tabular}{llll}
 & \(A\) & \(\overline A\) & Total \\ 
\(B\) & 90 & 30 & 120 \\ 
\(\overline B\) & 20 & 60 & 80 \\ 
Total & 110 & 90 & 200 \\ 
\end{tabular}\end{center} 
\(f(A)=110/200=55\%\). \(f_A(B)=90/110=9/11\approx81.82\%\).
\end{frame}
\begin{frame}{Completing a table from frequencies}
A headline announces “Three pass holders in four take the bus”, based on \(f_B(A)=75\%\). Explain the error and propose a correct sentence.
\end{frame}
\begin{frame}{Worked answer: Completing a table from frequencies}
The headline reverses the conditioning. The correct sentence is: “Three people in four among those who take the bus have a pass.” The proportion of pass holders who take the bus is here about \(81.82\%\).
\end{frame}
\begin{frame}[fragile]{Python}
\small
\begin{verbatim}
# Exemple fictif : (transport, satisfaction)
donnees = [("bus", "oui"), ("marche", "oui"),
           ("bus", "non"), ("velo", "oui"),
           ("bus", "oui"), ("marche", "non")]

bus = [r for r in donnees if r[0] == "bus"]
bus_satisfaits = [r for r in donnees
                 if r[0] == "bus" and r[1] == "oui"]
autres = [r for r in donnees if not r[0] == "bus"]
\end{verbatim}
\end{frame}
\begin{frame}{Processing a file and collecting real data}
Give the sizes of the three lists. Calculate the frequency of satisfaction among bus users. Replace \texttt{and} by \texttt{or} in the second filter: how many rows are then selected?
\end{frame}
\begin{frame}{Worked answer: Processing a file and collecting real data}
Sizes: \(3,2,3\). Among bus users, the frequency of satisfaction is \(2/3\). With \texttt{or}, we select the \(3\) bus users and the \(2\) satisfied people using another means: \(5\) rows, without counting twice the rows satisfying both criteria.
\end{frame}
\begin{frame}{Processing a file and collecting real data}
Collect anonymously two variables: main means of transport and journey time in ordered categories (\(<15\) min; from \(15\) to under \(30\) min; \(\geq30\) min). One row per response, without names. Construct the two-way table, then two conditional frequencies in opposite directions. State the count, the collection date and any non-responses.
\end{frame}
\begin{frame}{Processing a file and collecting real data}
Carry out the collection and write two justified conclusions. Explain why the results do not automatically describe all students in Madagascar.
\end{frame}
\begin{frame}{Worked answer: Processing a file and collecting real data}
The values depend on the actual collection. Check: one category per variable and per response; sum of the cells equal to the number of usable responses; correct denominator for each frequency; announced rounding. The sample is one particular class, not a representative sample of all students in the country. Non-responses must be distinguished from an observed category.
\end{frame}
